title: Working at Redwood — roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This page summarizes what it means to work at Redwood: our people philosophy, role families and career ladders, core benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding flow, and the primary internal tools all new hires should know. Intended audience: new employees, managers, interviewers, and partners who support hiring and onboarding.

1) Our people philosophy

- We hire engineers, product builders, and operators who are ownership-oriented, curious, and customer-centered.
- Career growth is a shared responsibility: employees own career goals; managers and People Ops provide coaching, opportunity, and clear evaluation criteria.
- We prioritize psychological safety, inclusion, and results: feedback should be timely, specific, and actionable.

2) Working at Redwood — what to expect

- Full-time employees follow a flexible remote-first policy with company hubs in key regions. Core collaboration hours are typically 10:00–16:00 local team time unless otherwise agreed.
- Team structure is cross-functional: product + eng + design + applied ML + SRE + sales/CS for customer-facing squads.
- Weekly rituals: team standups, product syncs, and a biweekly all-hands. Team-specific cadences (roadmaps, demos, retro) are listed on team pages.

3) Role families and career ladders (overview)

We maintain transparent ladders for major role families. Each ladder describes expectations across ownership, technical/functional skill, impact, mentorship, and scope. Managers and ICs use these ladders during calibration and promotion cycles.

Role families covered here: engineering (backend, infra, serving runtime), applied ML, product (PM), design, SRE/ops, sales & customer success, people-ops, and finance/legal.

Example ladder summary (IC engineering):

- Engineer I (E1): entry-level, delivers well-scoped work with guidance, learns codebase and systems.
- Engineer II (E2): owns features/modules, contributes to design, reliable deliverer.
- Senior Engineer (E3): leads end-to-end features, influences design across teams, mentors others.
- Staff Engineer (E4): drives architecture and cross-team initiatives, defines technical strategy.
- Principal/Distinguished (E5+): sets multi-product technical direction, visible external contributions, high mentorship and hiring impact.

Manager ladder (example):

- Manager I: supervises a small team, focuses on delivery and career development.
- Manager II: manages larger org slices, owns hiring plans and cross-team coordination.
- Director/Head: sets strategy for multiple teams, partner with exec leadership on roadmap.

Promotion & calibration process (high level):

1. Promotion readiness is discussed during 1:1s and tracked in people-ops templates.
2. Candidate packet (self-assessment + manager write-up + peer feedback) is assembled.
3. Calibration committee reviews packets quarterly; decisions communicated within two weeks of cycle.
4. Appeals/clarifications handled through your manager and People Ops.

4) Performance reviews and goal setting

- Cadence: annual performance review + mid-year check-in. Managers set OKRs with each individual quarterly.
- Criteria: impact, craft (technical/product skill), leadership & collaboration, and growth.
- Feedback: Redwood uses a mix of written feedback and calibration panels to ensure fairness across teams.

5) Compensation, equity, and leveling guidance

- Compensation components: base salary, annual bonus (if applicable), and equity grant at hire + refreshes. Total compensation philosophy is market-competitive with regional adjustments for cost-of-living.
- Pay review cadence: role changes, promotions, and annual comp refresh.
- Equity: standard 4-year vesting with 1-year cliff for full-time hires unless otherwise negotiated.

6) Benefits & perks (summary)

- Health & wellbeing:
  - Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contribution; multiple plan tiers to choose from.
  - Mental health support including counseling sessions and an EAP.
- Time off:
  - Unlimited PTO policy with a recommended minimum of 15 days/year for planning purposes; mandatory 3-week minimum parental leave for primary caregivers and 8 weeks for secondary caregivers (region-dependent).
  - 10 company holidays plus 1 floating day.
- Financial benefits:
  - 401(k) plan with company match (US) or local equivalent in other regions.
  - Competitive parental leave top-up policy (where applicable).
- Learning & growth:
  - $2,000/year individual learning stipend for courses, conferences, or books.
  - Regular lunch-and-learn sessions and a formal mentorship program.
- Productivity & home office:
  - New-hire equipment stipend and a recurring home-office allowance for remote employees.
  - Discounted coworking membership reimbursement in approved locations.
- Other perks:
  - Commuter benefits where offered, season ticket loans in select regions, and a discretionary employee referral bonus program.

7) Hiring process — quick reference

Overview (typical for IC roles):
1. Application / referral → recruiter screen (30 min).
2. Hiring manager screen (30–45 min) → take-home or project (role-dependent).
3. Onsite / loop: 3–5 interviews covering system design, core skills, and culture / collaboration.
4. Debrief and calibration → offer decision.
5. Offer and background checks → start date scheduling.

Interviewer guidelines (short):
- Evaluate to rubric: problem-solving, communication, technical skill, ownership, and cultural add.
- Provide timely written feedback within 48 hours.
- Disclose conflicts of interest to the recruiter.

Diversity & inclusion in hiring:
- All open roles are posted with inclusive language and salary ranges. Interview panels should strive for diverse perspectives. People Ops can help source diverse candidate pipelines.

8) Onboarding — 30/60/90 and checklist

New hire checklist (first week highlights):
- Pre-day 1: equipment delivered, Okta/SAML access configured, GitHub access requested, Slack invite, calendar holds for orientation.
- Day 1: People Ops orientation, benefits enrollment walkthrough, manager 1:1, team lunch.
- Week 1: complete required security & compliance trainings, read team docs, pair with a buddy, set initial 30/60/90 goals.

30/60/90 plan (recommended):
- 30 days: learn systems, ship a small bug/feature, meet key partners, complete onboarding trainings.
- 60 days: own a project milestone, participate in design reviews, contribute to team roadmap.
- 90 days: deliver a measurable outcome, present a retrospective on first project, discuss career goals and next steps with manager.

Manager responsibilities during onboarding:
- Schedule weekly 1:1s, set clear expectations, provide early feedback, assign a buddy, and ensure timely access to tools and environments.

9) Internal tools & access (core list)

- Identity & SSO: Okta (primary login portal) — use Okta for all app access and MFA.
- Communication: Slack — core channels by org, #announcements for company-wide updates.
- Documentation: Confluence — team and product docs; this handbook lives in the company-handbook space.
- Ticketing & roadmaps: Jira — create tickets for work; follow team-specific workflow.
- Source control: GitHub Enterprise — all code lives in org repositories; use protected branches for main and release.
- CI/CD: internal CI pipelines (see eng-infra/runbooks) — PR template and checklist required for prod changes.
- Access requests: internal access portal (submit an access request ticket) — managers approve role-based access.
- Redwood Console / Platform access: request environment and dataset access via the internal platform onboarding form; separate request for production key access with SLA.

Quick reference commands & tips:
- To request GitHub access: open an access ticket and cc your manager in the approval thread.
- For production environment access: follow the production access checklist in eng-sre/runbooks and complete training.

10) Escalations and key contacts

- People Ops (hiring, benefits, policy): people-ops@redwood.com.
- IT & device support: it-support@redwood.com.
- Security incidents: security@redwood.com (follow incident response runbook).
- Payroll & comp questions: payroll@redwood.com.

11) FAQs (short)

Q: Who approves time off?
A: Your direct manager approves PTO in the HR portal. For cross-team time off that affects launches, coordinate with your squad lead.

Q: How do I request career mentorship?
A: Talk to your manager and submit a mentorship request form to people-ops; we’ll match you with a mentor based on goals.

Q: Where are salary bands documented?
A: Salary ranges are available through people-ops and are reviewed during leveling conversations; managers can share the relevant band during calibration.

12) Related policies and resources

- Employee code of conduct (link on the policies page).
- Security & acceptable use policy (security-and-compliance).
- Parental leave and family-friendly policies (people-ops/policies).
- Role-specific ladders and detailed leveling rubrics: see team pages under company-handbook/roles-and-onboarding.

Feedback on this page

If you have suggestions or notice missing/incorrect information, please file a doc update request via the Confluence page comments or email people-ops@redwood.com.
